core.title: Use the plane keyword cues when routing an acceptance to a test-layer plane
core.given: An acceptance whose test-layer plane is being selected or reviewed
core.when: routing the acceptance to a test-layer plane
core.then: Use the plane keyword cues in the acceptance wording when selecting its plane.
prefer: Read the acceptance wording against the keyword -> plane cue table: ui: display, visible, screen, render, animation | ux: understand, clarity, steps, easy, confusing | be: validate, apply, compute, reconcile, rule | nw: request, response, timeout, websocket, stream | db: query, index, transaction, lock, row | st: asset, download, upload, cache, blob, cdn | tm: event, metrics, trace, ingest, drop | sc: schema, contract, version, field, json | au: login, token, permission, rate-limit, 403 | fn: price, balance, payout, token | if: cpu, memory, pod, node, gpu.
avoid: Selecting an acceptance's plane without consulting the keyword cues in its wording.
core.why: The source provides these keyword cues as the reference for selecting the test-layer plane when routing an acceptance.
evidence: For each routed acceptance, a reviewer can read the selected plane against the cue words in its wording and see that the cue table was consulted.
verification: For each routed acceptance, a check reads the selected plane against the cue words in the acceptance wording and the rule's keyword -> plane cue table. That table is the convention's own routing-table term plane_keywords ('keyword -> plane routing table.'): ui=[display, visible, screen, render, animation]; ux=[understand, clarity, steps, easy, confusing]; be=[validate, apply, compute, reconcile, rule]; nw=[request, response, timeout, websocket, stream]; db=[query, index, transaction, lock, row]; st=[asset, download, upload, cache, blob, cdn]; tm=[event, metrics, trace, ingest, drop]; sc=[schema, contract, version, field, json]; au=[login, token, permission, rate-limit, '403']; fn=[price, balance, payout, token]; if=[cpu, memory, pod, node, gpu].
'token' appears as a cue under both au and fn; a match on 'token' alone does not by itself distinguish those planes.
'403' is a string cue (quoted as a string in the source table), not a number; cue terms are compared as strings.
The cues are cues, not an exhaustive or deterministic routing algorithm: compliance means the cue table was consulted, not that a unique plane was derived from the wording.
Recognising that routing is happening, and whether wording semantically matches a cue (including how overlapping cues resolve), are judgment calls; a plain keyword scan is only a hint.
The task-term and change facts are optional discovery signals only, not required gates; routing an unchanged acceptance also fires.

values: acceptance wording contains a plane keyword cue

fires: A new acceptance is written and its test-layer plane must be selected.
The plane of an existing, unchanged acceptance is reviewed or re-checked, in any artifact type.
An acceptance whose wording contains cue words such as 'render', 'timeout', 'transaction' or 'permission' is being assigned a plane.
doesNotFire: Work that neither selects nor reviews the test-layer plane of any acceptance (e.g. implementing production code, editing text with no acceptances).

neutralityNotes: This planner-method rule is already stack-neutral: no item names a stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so nothing was rewritten or weakened. The plane taxonomy (ui, ux, be, nw, db, st, tm, sc, au, fn, if) and its keyword cue table, including the routing-table term identifier plane_keywords and its label 'keyword -> plane routing table.', are the convention's own canonical data carried verbatim from the source, so they remain in the core (prefer[0], named in verification) rather than being moved to the structure profile, which describes where things live and how they are shaped, not convention data; consequently profileRequirements is empty and nothing is Bun-specific, so bunOnly is empty. The activation fact 'note' fields cannot be represented in the core fact schema (fact/values/observability only), so their content is preserved in the fires/doesNotFire situations and the verification array.
